headline: unit+900h is an eight-value plane state enum and the shipped executable names it: 007CCB30's jump table at 007CCBC0 maps 0 "N/A plane state", 1 "Inside", 2 "Locked", 3 (no label, prints "huh?"), 4 "Runway", 5 "Runway on Path", 6 "Water", 7 "Flying". unit+908h is the airborne clock in seconds and unit+904h is "this ground contact followed a real flight", derived as clock > 5s on entering 4 or 5.

flight_state_enum.label: N/A plane state
flight_state_enum.meaning: the plane unit constructor's value; no motion arm matches

flight_state_enum.label: Inside
flight_state_enum.meaning: stowed inside the hangar or airbase

flight_state_enum.label: Locked
flight_state_enum.meaning: held on a launch spot; the setter cuts the throttle and the ground law passes 0.0f instead of 1.0f to the core law
launching (provisional): the setter forces the throttle to 1.0f and 007C6340 has a dedicated no-write arm for it

flight_state_enum.label: Runway
flight_state_enum.meaning: free ground roll on a runway or a deck

flight_state_enum.label: Runway on Path
flight_state_enum.meaning: ground roll driven along a path; no steering authority and no self-initiated takeoff

corrections.was: the motion dispatch's surface arm is gated on a second enum, "surface | unit+5F0h == 6 | 007CECAF 007CBA50", and the doc's open question asks what unit+900h's six values mean
corrections.is: the gate is unit+900h == 6, the Water value of the eight-value enum; there is no enum at unit+5F0h
corrections.evidence: in 007CEC30-007CECB4 EDI is the unit and ESI is unit+310h: 007CECB4 LEA ECX,[ESI+364h] feeds 0085DC80, which the same doc writes as unit+674h, and 007CEC30 MOV EDX,[ESI+41Ch] is its own unit+72Ch. 007CEC99 CMP dword ptr [ESI+5F0h],6 under the same bias is unit+900h == 6, and 007CEC4E FADD [ESI+5F8h] is unit+908h, the airborne clock the doc's own free-flight row describes

corrections.was: PlaneMotionDispatchInputs carries `int surface_mode{0}; // unit+5F0h` and select_motion_arm_007ce040 branches on it
corrections.is: the third arm branches on the same ground_water_mode field; select_motion_arm_007cec30 in include/bsp/plane_ground_ops.hpp supersedes it with two inputs
corrections.evidence: the same 007CEC99 reading as above. The header was not edited: it is not an owned file of this packet

corrections.was: the per-class gain table attributes `+1E0h WheelBrake` to the "ground arm"
corrections.is: WheelBrake is read in 007DB680 BSP_PlaneFlight_CoreLaw, the law all three arms share, not in the ground arm 007CBFA0 or the ground law 007DCCF0
corrections.evidence: a scan of every disp32 access at displacement 1E0h in .text finds exactly two: the class-field writer 007D22BD and the read 007DBEF6 FLD dword ptr [EAX+1E0h], whose containing function is 007DB680 (body 007DB680-007DC82A)

uncertainties: state 3 is named Launching from its side effects only: the shipped debug table has no label for it, and no routine was found that requests it. If nothing requests it the state is dead in the shipped build

unit+C01h has five writers (007B9000, 007B9010, 007CB37E, 007CC2AD, 007D0116) and no reader that a full disp32 scan of .text can see; the takeoff chain's third outcome therefore has no established consumer

docs/PLANE_FLIGHT.md records 007DA8D9 as discarding the roll term when ctl+FCh != 1. With ctl+FCh established as 0 in free flight, 1 on the ground and 2 on the water, that would confine the roll term to the ground roll; 007DA8D9 was not re-read
classDesc+1FCh, the reference the lift-off height test subtracts, has no key in docs/PLANE_CLASS_FIELDS.md and sits between the two GroundPitch slots +1F8h and +200h

the reading of MinWaterSpd as the flying-boat discriminator is consistent across four sites (the setter's 4/5 gate, the placement chooser, the submersion accumulator and the water law's floating arm) but was not cross-tabulated against the installed per-class values
the object at unit+DECh and the deck object reached as (unit+BF4h)->+4h->+3Ch are used by vtable slot only; neither was identified
run_time_evidence: none. bsp_game.exe has no path that reaches a plane on a deck or on the water, so no claim in this packet is supported by a run log and none is presented as run-time evidence.
